assertions: Sir William Waller will overcome Sir Ralph Hopton in the engagement near Alresford (Battle of Cheriton) on the day of the figure, 29 March 1644
Hopton's Royalist force will be defeated and forced to leave / retreat from the field, rather than Waller's Parliamentarians

Waller has the stronger and better-assisted army: his side's significators are dignified and supported, with the Sun, lord of his substance/assistants, angular in the 10th in the exact degree of his exaltation (19 degrees Aries)

Hopton has no ready supplies or effective assistance/seconding force available: only Mars and the South Node occupy the house of his supplies, and his significator Saturn receives no aspect from any planet

Hopton's significator Saturn is in his fall, peregrine and under the Sun's beams (sub radiis), square the cusp of his own 7th house, showing his side weakened, dishonoured and suffering the greater loss in this fight
The Moon, for Waller's side, in her exaltation with Jupiter, swift and increasing in light, shows Waller's fortune advancing swiftly to a same-day decisive advantage
method: Lilly classical horary astrology for a war question: 1st-house side versus 7th-house opponent, judged by essential/accidental dignity, angularity, aspects and assistance to the significators
reasoning: Waller's side (Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter and Venus) is dignified: Moon exalted and with benefic Jupiter, swift and increasing in light, and the Sun lord of Waller's substance/assistants is in the 10th in 19 Aries, the exact degree of exaltation, giving him strong, honourable assistance. Hopton's significator Saturn, lord of the 7th, is in direct contrast: in his fall, peregrine, sub radiis, in no aspect to any planet (no aid), and square his own 7th cusp, with no ready supplies (only Mars and the South Node in the supplies house). In Lilly's war rules the dignified, angular, assisted significator overcomes the fallen, peregrine, unaided one, so the 1st-house commander wins and the 7th-house commander is routed.
summary: Waller will overcome Hopton at Cheriton/Alresford on 29 March 1644; Hopton will be defeated and retreat.
